presets.name: Prepositional-phrase attachment
presets.description: A small English fragment where a prepositional phrase can modify either a noun phrase (NP -> NP PP) or a verb phrase (VP -> VP PP). Both rules are left-recursive. Each extra PP multiplies the readings: 1 PP gives 2 parses, 2 PPs give 5, 3 PPs give 14 (Catalan numbers).

presets.name: Coordination and modifier scope
presets.description: Does "old" describe only the men, or the men and the women? The rule NP -> NP Conj NP lets a coordination sit inside or outside a modified noun phrase, so the grammar finds both scopes.

presets.name: Optional elements (empty rules)
presets.description: Determiners and adjectives are optional here, written with ε (the empty string). The parser handles empty rules with the Aycock and Horspool technique: when it predicts a symbol that can be empty, it also moves past it straight away.

presets.name: Ambiguous arithmetic
presets.description: A classic from computer science. Without precedence rules, "n + n * n" has two trees, one for (n + n) * n and one for n + (n * n). Grammars of programming languages avoid this ambiguity; natural language cannot.
